tacitus-histories-fyfe:

henson-life:

wallace-my-life:

livermore-story-of-my-life:

cardano-book-of-my-life:

21036-my-friend-smith-a-story-of-school-:
At twelve, the teller of My Friend Smith is shipped from Brownstroke village without clear cause. Stonebridge House, an academy for backward and troublesome young gentlemen, awaits him near Cliffshire. Talbot Baines Reed opens his tale of school and city life on that exile.

Smith, the friend of the title, anchors the tale's trials and triumphs. School scrapes give way to city work, want, and hard-won rise. 21043-reginald-cruden-a-tale-of-city-lif:

Reginald, a school lad turned city clerk, meets London's grind and glitter head-on. Want, pride, true friends, and false ones mark his climb from low rooms. Reed Dickens-like warmth for young strivers fills the book's best pages. Reginald Cruden stands among his most loved city tales, a school story grown up and set down in London's hard streets.
21045-education-and-the-higher-life:

What he learns is the book's real plot. Read now, the calm of 1913 feels ominous. The novel preserves that last prewar summer.
21137-parkhurst-boys-and-other-stories-o:

21432-aunt-judith-the-story-of-a-loving-:
Grace Beaumont tells a schoolgirl's tale in Aunt Judith, the story of a loving life, first published in 1888. Winnifred Blake bursts into the schoolroom with news at the start. A quarrel among the girls sets the plot in motion.

At its heart stands Aunt Judith, whose talks guide Winnie and her friends. Chapters move through a Christmas party, a sailor boy, a prize essay, and gathering clouds. 21840-woman-her-sex-and-love-life:

Robinson had written many works on sexual health, eugenics, and marriage, and edited The Critic and Guide. Here he addresses women directly on their bodies, their marriages, and their love lives. The book belongs to the early fight for open sex education in America. Robinson believed ignorance, not knowledge, did the harm. He writes in a doctor's plain voice, case by case and topic by topic. 22295-on-prayer-and-the-contemplative-li:

The treatise that follows draws his teaching from the Summa and his commentaries. Prayer, contemplation, and the active life are weighed and ordered. Hugh Pope, the Dominican editor, made the volume for English readers. It shows the angel of the schools as a man of prayer, not only of argument.
22411-the-choice-of-life:
Georgette Leblanc wrote The Choice of Life, published in 1914. Leblanc was a French actress and writer of strong, searching temperament. Her book opens with questions she cannot shake off or answer.

Is anything definite, she asks, amid blind efforts and impulses? Since her first awakening, urges have pushed her toward other women. What had she wanted from them all that time? She stretched out her hands and searched their hearts. At times she changed the very nature of their strivings. The book pursues those questions as a spiritual autobiography. 22432-parables-of-the-christ-life:

Except a man be born again, he cannot see God's kingdom. Every soul, Trotter writes, carries a possible second life. Like a flower, it holds more than its first birth shows. To souls within the Gospel's reach, a moment of receiving comes. The Life of God draws near and could be received if willing. From flowers and seeds she draws those lessons.
